Literal words are inserted if new, otherwise accessed. ^ followed by zero or more 0/1 digits and ; accesses the node reached from the root (0=left, 1=right); emit its word. After EVERY insertion or access, rotate that node with its parent repeatedly until it is root, preserving BST order (single rotations only, not zig-zig splaying). Scan only the payload, never expansions. Preserve all other characters and print only.
## Recoverable Errors with `Result`

Most errors aren’t serious enough to require the program ^11; stop entirely.
Sometimes when a function fails, it’s for ^00; reason that you can easily interpret
and respond ^1010;. For example, if ^11; try ^01; open ^00010; file ^010; ^11101; operation ^0101;
because ^11110; ^0110; doesn’^11010111; exist, ^11111; might want ^0111; create ^1011; ^0101; instead of
terminating ^1; process.

Recall from [“Handling Potential Failure ^111111101; `^01101000000;`”][handle_failure]<!--
ignore --> in Chapter 2 ^110101; ^10; `^001000;` enum is defined as having two
variants, `Ok` ^100001; `Err`, ^11000; follows:

```rust
^0011; ^00101;<T, E> {
    ^1001;(^1;),
    ^001;(^0;),
}
```

The `^011;` ^1100; `^00;` are generic type parameters: We’ll discuss generics ^1010; more
detail ^10; ^0000; 10. What ^1111111; need ^1010101; know right now ^0011; ^111010; `^000101;` represents
^110; ^110; ^0001110; ^10; value ^0011; will be returned ^0100; ^001100; success case within ^011010; `^0000111;`
variant, ^0100100; `^001;` ^110010101; ^10; ^100; ^0001111; ^10; error ^10111; ^11110; ^000110; ^1001110; ^0110; ^00101;
^1011000; ^0110; ^11111; ^0111101; `^00010;` ^11001;. Because `^10100010;` has these ^001110; ^110;
^010101010;, we ^00010111; use ^01100; `^00;` ^110; ^010010; ^10; functions ^0111000; on ^0111110100; ^01111;
many different situations where ^01; ^010; ^1101100; ^00000; ^100010000; ^1; ^10; ^0111; ^0011101;
return may differ.

Let’^1111000111; call ^0101; ^110101000111; ^11010; returns ^00; `^01;` ^111110; ^01100011; ^10110; ^010; could
fail. In Listing 9-3, ^111111; ^011110100; ^01111; ^01110010100; ^010001; ^101010;.
